newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps all edge higher, bar flat naphtha.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps all edge higher, bar flat naphtha.

text.p: European oil swaps were generally firmer on Tuesday bar steady naphtha which appeared to be resistant to crude's latest recovery.

Brent CFDs edged up 10 cents or so with the balance of this week pegged around -47 cents against August Brent from -56/57 cents on Monday while next week, June 23-27 showed a stronger gain to -35 cents from -49/50 cents.
Further out the gains were less sharp with June 30-July 4 hovering around -35 cents against August from -45 cents with July 7-11 assessed at -33/34 from -40 cents.
June 30-July 4 traded at August -33 cents and July 7-11 was concluded at -33 cents.

Heavy fuel swaps tacked up nearly $1 a tonne with July hovering around $83.50, August at $84.25 and September at $84.50. On the wet side barges traded at $84 and $84.50 fob and at least five times at $86.
Dealers said the market was in the $85-86 range with the lower numbers possibly linked to pricing an incoming cargo.
Low sulphur fuel swaps were unchanged in a $91.50 to $92.00 range for July with August and September marginally in contango.
Gas oil crack spreads held steady for 4Q at $4.55 with 1Q98 also broadly unchanged at a touch under $4.60.
Gasoline swaps were about $1 stronger at $185.50/186.00 for July with August about 50 cents backwardated and September a further $1 weaker.
Naphtha was unchanged with July, August and September all pretty flat around $179-180.
